clue.text: Frenchwoman forced to dress before PM

indicators.note: one word wearing another around it, as clothes go round a body, so it is wrapped around

parts.note: made, as in made to do something, means forced
the morning hours before post meridiem are a.m.

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is compelled to get dressed before the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dress' means the word for forced is worn around the morning letters, splitting it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title and form of address for a married woman.

clue.text: Evil man's first order?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word man's is wanted here

parts.note: to order things is to align or arrange them neatly

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man's first command was a wicked one.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign is an adjective meaning wicked or harmful in intent, a synonym of evil.

clue.text: Record, then forget to include loud rattle

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the word for forget takes the next piece within itself

parts.note: to omit something is to forget or leave it out
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Instructions to put on a record and stop bothering with a noisy rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts F inside OMIT to make OMFIT. 'rattle' looks like a noun but is the verb, to unsettle.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to unsettle or disconcert them, just as rattling them does.

clue.text: Almost ruin everything after wedding

parts.note: to mar something is to ruin or spoil it

indicators.note: almost the whole phrase is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: it all is an everyday phrase for everything

explanation.surface: Someone almost wrecks everything just after the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruin everything = MAR IT ALL; 'Almost' drops its final L. 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, wedding relates to marriage, as in wedding vows, which are marital vows.

clue.text: Plant needs a container like this

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A plant needs to be housed in a pot of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean perennial with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian column carvings.

clue.text: New London location has bridge over one canal

parts.note: to bridge two things is to connect them
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cut is a man-made waterway, a canal

explanation.surface: A description of a new part of London with a bridge crossing a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New London' looks like fresh development in the British capital, but it is a city in the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: New London is a port city in the US state of Connecticut, so the state locates it.

clue.text: Risk following extremely nice traveller

indicators.note: the word for risk comes after the other piece
only the extreme letters, at both ends, of nice are taken

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a risk taken on an outcome

explanation.surface: A very pleasant traveller takes a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters N and E of 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age travellers are a British subculture of nomads, so a New Ager is such a traveller.

clue.text: What about river flowing for bird?

indicators.note: turned about, the word for what is read in reverse

parts.note: eh? is a request to repeat, meaning what?
on means in progress, moving along

explanation.surface: A question about a river running for a bird to fish in.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird that fishes in rivers.

clue.text: Frank's mouth mostly visible?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that visible must be read as in sight, so the clipped mouth word goes in the word sight

parts.note: something visible is in sight; sight is the word the clipped mouth goes in

indicators.note: most of the word, all but its final letter, is used

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A question whether one frank fellow's mouth is largely on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visible' does double duty: read as IN SIGHT it gives both the container and the instruction to insert. Trap is slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and direct, as frank talk is straight talk.

clue.text: Craving Romeo, closer to Charlie Sheen

parts.note: lust is a strong craving
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its last letter, here of Charlie

explanation.surface: Charlie Sheen the actor, hungry for a Romeo role, edges closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie Sheen' looks like the actor, but Sheen is the definition and only the last letter of Charlie counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft glow or shine on a surface, synonymous with sheen.

clue.text: Rare news about one coming back?

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Unusual news concerning someone returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who replies, especially one who comes back with a retort, is one coming back.

clue.text: Engineer gets to do a refinement

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An engineer has some refining work to carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is discernment in style and manners, a kind of refinement.

clue.text: Defect in aspirin?

parts.note: aspiring, meaning coming as in up-and-coming, cut short by its final letter, makes the word in the clue

explanation.surface: A question whether there is a flaw in the painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: COMING (aspiring) made SHORT gives ASPIRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming is a failing or flaw, a synonym of defect.

clue.text: Spirits and dope used by team

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
a football or cricket team is eleven, written 11, which looks like two letter I

explanation.surface: A team uses alcohol and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Teams have eleven players, and 11 is read as the letters II.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie or genius, the spirits of Arabian tales.

clue.text: See finished

parts.note: to follow is to see or understand
through means finished, done

explanation.surface: An instruction to see a task through to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow through is to continue an action until it is completed.

clue.text: Sun's out — villain's stolen the safe

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the word sun, with the 's read as is, so the sun is out of order

indicators.note: the villain has taken the word the into himself

parts.note: a cad is a villain, a scoundrel; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: With the sun gone, a criminal has made off with the safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' marks an anagram of SUN, with the apostrophe s read as is; 'stolen' puts THE in CAD. 'safe' looks like a strongbox but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means unharmed, coming through without injury, so safe.

clue.text: Tidy up main Blackpool station?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: smart means neat and tidy
top means chief, the main one

explanation.surface: An instruction to clean up the main station in Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SMART into TRAMS. Blackpool, a seaside resort in Lancashire, is famous for its trams.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool keeps Britain's oldest tramway, so a stop on it is a station there.

clue.text: What we'd buy to go to see ABBA?

definitions.text: What we'd buy to go to see ABBA?

parts.words: What we'd buy to go to see ABBA?
parts.note: ABBA reads as a trip from A to B and then from B back to A, which needs tickets both ways

explanation.surface: What fans would purchase to attend a concert by the Swedish pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: ABBA looks like the band but reads as a journey A to B, then B back to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickets covering an outward trip and the trip back are what a journey there and home again requires.

clue.text: Diatribe about priest having faith?

indicators.note: the rant goes about, around, the priest

parts.note: a rant is a diatribe
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A tirade about a priest who has religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having faith' looks religious, but means trusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reliant means depending on or trusting, so having faith in someone or something.

clue.text: Implement used in kitchen for cereal

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words kitchen for cereal

explanation.surface: A utensil used in the kitchen for cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' looks like a noun, a tool, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule or law is to implement it, putting it into effect.

clue.text: Likely lad, initially single

indicators.note: the piece for single comes first, ahead of lad

parts.note: odd means single, not one of a pair, as an odd sock
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: A probable young man, who is single to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is odds-on is the favourite, so it is likely to win.

clue.text: Big noise from a bump in the snow

definitions.meaning: an important, powerful person, a magnate
a mound of hard snow on a ski slope

explanation.surface: A loud sound coming from a lump on a ski run.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a tycoon and a hump on a piste share this word, from different origins.

clue.text: Pass wolf

definitions.meaning: a narrow valley or ravine through mountains
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a ravine route through hills and a verb for eating greedily.

clue.text: Too much from labourer

parts.note: out of means from, as in made out of
a hand is a manual worker, a labourer

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a worker's demands are excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of hand has gone beyond control, become excessive.

clue.text: Reptile quietly burrows into ground

indicators.note: the quiet letter digs into the land word, going inside it

parts.note: terrain is ground, land
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A reptile silently digs down into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, a reptile.

clue.text: Romantic German supports protecting the Queen

indicators.note: the supports wrap round and shield the royal letters

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A German romantic backs a move to defend the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' is the period in music, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms was a nineteenth-century German composer of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Superior, like old Top Gear programme, ultimately

parts.note: early Top Gear came before its masked test driver, the Stig, so it was pre-Stig

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of programme

explanation.surface: A boast that something is superior, like a classic episode of the BBC motoring show.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring show; its anonymous racing driver is called the Stig.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, prestige means high-status, as in a prestige car, so superior.

clue.text: Joint blocked by dead tissue

indicators.note: the joint word is stopped up by the dead letter set inside it

parts.note: a tenon is part of a mortise and tenon woodworking joint

explanation.surface: A joint obstructed by dead tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a band of fibrous tissue linking muscle to bone.
